Grid Maxxing  ·  #1
The busiest hour

Every grid is built for its busiest hour. The cable into a building and the transformer down the street are both sized for the peak, and most hours they carry a fraction of it. A typical Swedish commercial building uses 20 to 35 percent of its grid connection on average. It pays for all of it, every month.

The busiest hour also sets the bill. In Sweden, grid fees rose 10.6 percent in 2025, the largest increase in 30 years. For a commercial building, the demand charge, set by its highest peaks, is 15 to 25 percent of what it pays for electricity. And if it needs a bigger connection for chargers or heat pumps, the wait in Europe can be two to ten years.

So the cheapest new capacity is the capacity already in the ground. A battery is the simplest way to use it. It charges when the building is quiet and covers the peaks when it is busy. The grid sees a smaller peak, and the bill follows. The room left over can carry the chargers.

That is Grid Maxxing: get far more out of the grid we have while the new grid gets built. It is the short version of our Master Plan, which starts from one line: build the grid for an electric civilization, build it from the nodes.

Energy is becoming abundant. Power remains scarce.
Where we do it

Buildings now, parks next

The next sites are bigger, and the ones I think about most are not buildings at all.

A wind or solar park has the same problem the other way around. Its connection is built for full output, but the weather decides when that comes. When the wind drops or the sun sets, the cable sits idle. When every park produces at once, power gets cheap, sometimes cheaper than free: parts of Sweden had several hundred hours of negative prices in 2025. A battery on the park’s own connection stores power when it is worth little and delivers it when it is needed. Same cable, different hours.

We design, install and run it, and we can bring the financing.

Two kinds of reader I want to hear from this month:

•  You own or develop wind or solar parks.

•  You run a site with sharp peaks and a grid bill that keeps climbing: a cold store, a factory, a depot getting truck chargers.

Reply to this email. If that is not you but you know who it is, forward it.
The home  ·  FTW

The open half

In the plan’s words, we open what should become ubiquitous and operate what requires trust. FTW is what we open: open source energy management for homes with solar, batteries and EV charging, running on your own hardware.

Are we in control? A command sent is not power moved. FTW now checks every battery, charger, solar limit and V2X link it controls, and gives one answer per device: is it doing what FTW asked? It compares fresh device readings with the command and confirms the change on the home’s own grid meter. If a battery stops following, FTW warns you within 30 seconds. If a device goes silent, it raises an alarm. I have not seen another home system do this.

A state-of-the-art planner, on a Pi. The Energy Planner is our own optimizer for a home’s battery, solar and car charging. It runs locally on a Raspberry Pi and comes free for home use with FTW. This month’s update gets much closer to the best possible plan in the same time. On real plans from my own home, in all 19 cases where the car could not charge, it now finds the best plan.

The thinking  ·  Coordinated with Fredrik
THE FALL: the day the grid stopped
▶  THE FALL, THE FILM · 13 MIN
On 28 April 2025, Spain and Portugal went dark. The grid lost 31 gigawatts, and around 50 million people were without power. THE FALL tells that day from the control rooms, as a thirteen-minute film. It is scored, and the sound that stops when the power does is the point of the whole thing.
Watch the film, 13 min →
If you want the why, the film is cut from three podcast episodes:

• The Height of the Fall PART I: why anything happens at all.

• In Step PART II: how a continent became one machine, and what holds it together.

• Twenty-Seven Seconds PART III: second by second, and what it takes to start a dead grid.

The podcast is “Coordinated with Fredrik”, on every platform.
